- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overshoot — cap upward trend correction at +5% of recent peak or adjust downward by 1–2% per day.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model overcorrects downward — offset by 1–2% upward bias to account for policy-induced volatility.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model underestimates upside — add 0.5–1% upward bias to forecast mean.  
- If model forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), reduce slope by 10–20% to reflect momentum decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is bearish and supply net is negative, model underestimates downside — add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- If recent auction events are frequent (e.g., 3+ auctions in 30d), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast volatility by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
